subQuestions.questionText:
Jericho Carpets opened a new branch in another province to distribute their carpets. This type of intensive strategy is known as …
A. product development.
B. product modification.
C. market penetration.
D. market development.
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: D (2 marks)
Market development involves entering new geographical markets/areas with existing products, which is exactly what Jericho Carpets did by opening a branch in another province.

subQuestions.questionText:
Amandla Distributors has no control over challenges posed by the … environment.
A. macro
B. micro
C. market
D. micro and market
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: A (2 marks)
The macro environment is uncontrollable; businesses cannot control its challenges (e.g. PESTLE factors). The micro environment is fully controllable, and the market environment is partially controllable (influenceable).

subQuestions.questionText:
The purpose of an interview is to …
A. book and prepare the venue.
B. invite possible candidates to apply for the vacancy.
C. determine a candidate's suitability for the job.
D. prepare responses for possible questions.
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: C (2 marks)
The primary purpose of an interview is to determine a candidate's suitability for the job. The other options are either preparation steps or part of recruitment, not the purpose of the interview itself.

options.B: invite possible candidates to apply for the vacancy.
options.C: determine a candidate's suitability for the job.

subQuestions.questionText:
Aziza Manufacturing Ltd uses … to reduce the cost of redundancy in the long run.

Quality circles are small groups of workers who voluntarily meet to discuss and solve work-related problems, including ways to reduce the cost of redundancy in the long run.

subQuestions.memoText:

Backward vertical integration is when a business takes over its supplier (upstream in the supply chain). Ranzo Furniture taking over Green Timber, their wood supplier, is an example of backward vertical integration.

The Employment Equity Act has implications for the HR function as it ensures that affirmative action measures are correctly implemented to redress historical inequities in employment.

subQuestions.questionText:
Complete the following statement by using the word(s) provided in the list below: backward; Employment Equity; opportunity; parental; quality control; family responsibility; quality assurance; strength; forward; Labour Relations.

Greywater Systems implements … to ensure that the required standards are met at every stage of the production process.
subQuestions.memoText:

Quality assurance focuses on ensuring required standards are met at every stage of the production process (process-focused), as opposed to quality control which is end-of-line inspection.

subQuestions.questionText: Discuss the rights of employers in terms of the Labour Relations Act (LRA), 1995 (Act 66 of 1995).
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 1 mark for fact + 1 mark for explanation (2 marks per complete right). Max 6 marks.

Employers have the right to:
- form employer organisations (1) to represent them in labour related matters. (1)
- form bargaining councils (1) for collective bargaining purposes. (1)
- lockout employees (1) who engage in labour action/an unprotected/illegal strike. (1)
- dismiss employees (1) who engage in an unprotected/illegal strike/misconduct such as intimidation/violence during a strike action. (1)
- not pay/remunerate employees who have participated in a protected strike (1) for services/work they did not do during the strike. (1)
- Any other relevant answer related to rights of employers in terms of the LRA.

subQuestions.questionText: Describe any TWO types of defensive strategies.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks per strategy type heading + 1 mark per relevant description (Submax 3 per strategy). Mark first TWO only. Max 6 marks.

Divestiture (2)
- Disposing/Selling some assets/divisions that are no longer profitable/productive. (1)
- Selling off divisions/product lines with slow growth potential. (1)
- Decreasing the number of shareholders by selling ownership. (1)
- Paying off debts by selling unproductive assets. (1)
- Withdrawing/Divesting their investment share in another business. (1)
Submax (3)

Retrenchment (2)
- Terminating the employment contracts/Letting go of employees for operational/structural/restructuring reasons/reduce costs/expenses. (1)
- Decreasing the number of product lines/Closing certain departments may result in some workers becoming redundant. (1)
Submax (3)

Liquidation (2)
- Selling all assets/Bringing the business activities to an end due to the inability to repay creditors/bankruptcy/lack of capital. (1)
- Selling the entire business in order to pay shareholders a fair price for their shares. (1)
- Allowing creditors to apply for forced liquidation in order to have their claims settled. (1)
- Companies in financial distress/difficulty may appeal for business rescue to avoid liquidation. (1)
Submax (3)

NOTE: Mark the first TWO (2) only.
Max (6)

subQuestions.questionText:

Compensation for Occupational Injuries and Diseases Amendment Act/COIDA (2)

subQuestions.questionText: Explain other advantages of the Act identified in QUESTION 2.6.1 for businesses.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 1 mark for fact + 1 mark for explanation (2 marks per complete advantage). Max 4 marks.

Other advantages of COIDA:
- Promotes health and safety of employees (1) which reduces accidents in the workplace. (1)
- Employees do not contribute towards this fund, (1) which improves morale in the workplace. (1)
- Claiming processes are relatively simple, (1) resulting in timeous pay-outs. (1)
- Eliminates time and costs (1) spent on lengthy civil court proceedings. (1)
- Any compensation to an employee/the family (1) is exempt from income tax. (1)
- Employers are protected from financial burden (1) should an accident occur in the workplace provided that the employer was not negligent. (1)
- Makes businesses more socially responsible (1) as they cannot just employ workers at random in dangerous working conditions. (1)
- Workers are treated with dignity and respect (1) as businesses view them as valuable assets and not just as workers. (1)
- Covers all employees at the workplace (1) if both parties meet all the necessary safety provisions in the Act. (1)
- Creates a framework (1) for acceptable employment practices and safety regulations. (1)
- Supply administrative guidelines/mechanisms (1) for dealing with/processing claims. (1)
- Employees are compensated financially (1) for any injury/disability resulting from performing their duties at their workplace. (1)
- In the event of the death of an employee as a result of a work-related accident/disease, (1) his/her dependent(s) will receive financial support. (1)
- Employees receive medical assistance (1) provided there is no other medical assistance option. (1)
- Medical expenses/Other types of compensation are paid to employees and/or their families (1) depending on the type/severity of the injuries. (1)
- Any other relevant answer related to other advantages of COIDA for businesses.

NOTE:
1. Do not award marks for 'monthly contributions to a common fund to protect workers in the event of workplace accidents'.
2. Accept relevant facts if the Act was incorrectly identified as an answer in QUESTION 2.6.1.
Max (4)

subQuestions.questionText: Advise businesses on the strategic management process.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks per complete step (1 mark for incomplete/phrase). Max 6 marks. Either Option may be used.

OPTION 1
- Have a clear vision/mission statement/measurable/realistic objective in place. (2)
- Identify opportunities/weaknesses/strengths/threats by conducting environmental scanning/situational analysis. (2)
- Tools available for environmental scanning may include a SWOT analysis/Porter's Five Forces model/PESTLE analysis/industrial analysis tools. (2)
- Formulate alternative strategies to respond to the challenges. (2)
- Develop (an) action plan(s), including the tasks to be done/deadlines to be met/resources to be procured. (2)
- Implement selected strategies by communicating it to all stakeholders/organising business resources/motivating staff. (2)
- Continuously evaluate/monitor/measure strategies in order to take corrective action. (2)
- Any other relevant answer related to the strategic management process.

OR

OPTION 2
- Review/Analyse/Re-examine their vision/mission statement. (2)
- Conduct an environmental analysis using models such as SWOT/PESTLE/Porter's Five Forces. (2)
- Formulate a strategy, such as a defensive/retrenchment strategy. (2)
- Implement a strategy, using a template such as an action plan. (2)
- Control/Evaluate/Monitor the implemented strategy to identify gaps/deviations in implementation. (2)
- Take corrective action to ensure goals/objectives are met. (2)
- Any other relevant answer related to the strategic management process.
Max (6)

subQuestions.questionText: Explain the benefits of induction for businesses.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 1 mark for fact + 1 mark for explanation (2 marks per complete benefit). Max 6 marks.

Benefits of induction:
- Allows new employees to settle in quickly (1) and work effectively. (1)
- Ensures that new employees understand the rules (1) and restrictions in the business. (1)
- New employees may establish relationships (1) with fellow employees at different levels. (1)
- Make new employees feel at ease in the workplace, (1) which reduces anxiety/insecurity/fear. (1)
- The results obtained during the induction process (1) provide a base for focussed training. (1)
- Increases quality of performance/productivity (1) which promotes the effective use of working methods/resources. (1)
- Minimises/Decreases the need for on-going training (1) and development. (1)
- Employees will be familiar with organisational structures, (1) such as who are their supervisors/low level managers. (1)
- Opportunities are created for new employees (1) to experience/explore different departments. (1)
- New employees will understand their role/responsibilities (1) concerning safety regulations and rules. (1)
- New employees will know the layout of the building/factory/offices where everything is (1) which saves production time. (1)
- Learn more about the business so that new employees understand their roles/responsibilities (1) in order to be more efficient. (1)
- Company policies regarding conduct/procedures/safety and security/employment contract/conditions of employment/working hours/leave (1) are communicated. (1)
- Realistic expectations for new employees, (1) as well as the business are created. (1)
- New employees may feel part of the team (1) resulting in positive morale/motivation. (1)
- Employees may have a better understanding of business policies (1) regarding ethical/professional conduct/procedures/CSR. (1)
- Reduces the staff turnover (1) as new employees have been inducted properly. (1)
- Any other relevant answer related to the benefits of induction for businesses.
Max (6)

subQuestions.questionText: Discuss the selection procedure as a human resources activity.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 1 mark for fact + 1 mark for explanation (2 marks per complete step). Max 6 marks. Either Option may be used. Procedure may be in any order.

OPTION 1
- Determine fair assessment criteria (1) on which selection will be based. (1)
- Applicants must submit the application forms/curriculum vitae (1) and certified copies of personal documents/IDs/proof of qualifications. (1)
- Sort the received documents/CVs (1) according to the assessment/selection criteria. (1)
- Screen/Determine which applications meet the minimum job requirements (1) and separate these from the rest. (1)
- Preliminary interviews are conducted (1) if many suitable applications were received/to identify suitable applicants. (1)
- Reference checks/Vetting process should be made (1) to verify the content of CVs/regarding work experience/criminal records/qualifications. (1)
- Compile a shortlist (1) of potential candidates identified. (1)
- Shortlisted candidates may be subjected (1) to various types of selection tests such as skills tests. (1)
- Invite shortlisted candidates (1) for an interview. (1)
- A written offer is made (1) to the selected candidate. (1)
- Inform unsuccessful applicants (1) about the outcome of their application. (1)/Some advertisements indicate the deadline (1) for informing only successful candidates. (1)
- Any other relevant answer related to the selection procedure as a human resources activity.

OR

OPTION 2
- Receive documentation such as application forms (1) and sort it according to the criteria of the job. (1)
- Evaluate CVs (1) and create a shortlist/screen the applicants. (1)
- Check information in the CVs (1) and contact references. (1)
- Conduct preliminary sifting interviews (1) to identify applicants who are not suitable for the job, although they meet all requirements. (1)
- Assess/Test candidates (1) who have applied for senior positions/to ensure the best candidate is chosen. (1)
- Conduct interviews (1) with shortlisted candidates. (1)
- Offer employment in writing (1) to the selected candidate(s). (1)
- Any other relevant answer related to the selection procedure as a human resources activity.

NOTE: The procedure may be in any order.
Max (6)

subQuestions.questionText: Evaluate the impact of adequate financing and capacity as a total quality management (TQM) element on large businesses.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 1 mark for fact + 1 mark for explanation (2 marks per complete impact). Max 6 marks. Positive and/or negative responses accepted.

Positives/Advantages
- Large businesses have sufficient financing (1) to test everything before implementing. (1)
- They can afford to have systems in place (1) to prevent errors in processes/defects in raw materials/products. (1)
- Able to afford product research/market researchers (1) to gather information about products/customers. (1)/Large businesses can fund programmes (1) aimed at improving quality processes. (1)

Negatives/Disadvantages
- If the demand for a business product increases/orders begins coming in faster than expected, (1) the business may lack the capital required to fund the production of the stock/to fill the orders. (1)

Secondary sector (2)
(Manufacturing of products from raw materials falls under the secondary sector.)

subQuestions.questionText:
Identify the business sector applicable to the statement below.

Mountain Traders sell sports equipment to different sports outlets.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks for the correct sector.

Tertiary sector (2)
(Selling/distribution/services to retailers falls under the tertiary sector.)

subQuestions.questionText: Discuss the penalties for non-compliance with the Employment Equity Act (EEA), 1998 (Act 55 of 1998).
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 1 mark for fact + 1 mark for explanation (2 marks per complete penalty). Max 6 marks.

Penalties for non-compliance with EEA:
- Businesses may face heavy fines (1) for non-compliance. (1)
- They can be ordered to pay compensation/damages (1) to the employee for unfair discrimination. (1)
- Labour inspectors may conduct onsite visits/interview employees (1) to determine whether the information supplied on the employment equity plans is true or has been falsified. (1)
- Labour inspectors may investigate/inspect/ask questions about complaints (1) which can create a bad image for the business. (1)
- A compliance order may be issued to businesses (1) that do not comply with the EEA. (1)
- Businesses may be brought before the Labour Court (1) if compliance orders are not adhered to/no efforts made to reach targets. (1)
- The Department of Labour may block non-compliant businesses (1) from doing business with the government/receiving government tenders. (1)
- Any other relevant answer related to penalties for non-compliance with the EEA.
Max (6)

subQuestions.questionText: Advise businesses on the steps in strategy evaluation.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks per complete step (1 mark for phrase). Max 6 marks. Steps may be in any order.

Steps in strategy evaluation:
- Examine the underlying basis of a business strategy. (2)
- Look forward and backwards into the implementation process. (2)
- Compare the expected performance with the actual performance. (2)
- Determine the reasons for deviations and analyse these reasons. (2)
- Take corrective action so that deviations may be corrected. (2)
- Set specific dates for control and follow up. (2)
- Draw up a table of the advantages and disadvantages of a strategy. (2)
- Decide on the desired outcome that will result in the achievement of business goals envisaged when strategies are implemented. (2)
- Consider the impact of the strategic implementation in the internal/external environments of the business. (2)
- Any other relevant answer related to the steps in strategy evaluation.

NOTE: The steps may be in any order.
Max (6)

subQuestions.questionText: Outline the legal requirements of an employment contract.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks per complete requirement (1 mark for phrase). Max 4 marks.

Legal requirements of an employment contract:
- The employer and employee/Both parties must sign the contract. (2)
- Employer and employee must agree to any changes to the contract. (2)
- No party may unilaterally change aspects of the employment contract. (2)
- The remuneration package, including benefits, must be clearly indicated. (2)
- The employment contract may not contain any requirements that are in conflict with the BCEA. (2)
- Aspects of the employment contract can be renegotiated during the course of employment. (2)
- The employer must explain the terms and conditions of the employment contract to the employee. (2)
- Conditions of employment/duties/responsibilities of the employees must be stipulated clearly. (2)
- All business policies/procedures/disciplinary codes/rules can form part of the employment contract. (2)
- The employer must allow the employee to thoroughly read through the contract before it is signed. (2)
- The employment contract should include a code of conduct and code of ethics. (2)
- Any other relevant answer related to the legal requirements of an employment contract.
Max (4)

subQuestions.questionText: Explain the impact of fringe benefits on businesses.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 1 mark for fact + 1 mark for explanation (2 marks per complete impact). Max 6 marks. Positive and/or negative accepted.

Positives/Advantages
- Attractive fringe benefit packages (1) may result in higher employee retention/reduces employee turnover. (1)
- Attracts qualified/skilled/experienced employees (1) who may positively contribute towards the business goals/objectives. (1)
- Improves productivity (1) resulting in higher profitability. (1)
- It increases employee satisfaction/loyalty, (1) as they may be willing to go the extra mile. (1)
- Businesses save money (1) as benefits are tax deductible. (1)
- Fringe benefits can be used as leverage (1) for salary negotiations. (1)
- Any other relevant answer related to positive impact/advantages of fringe benefits on businesses.

AND/OR

Negatives/Disadvantages
- Businesses which cannot offer fringe benefits, (1) fail to attract skilled workers. (1)
- Businesses which offer employees different benefit plans (1) may create resentment (1)/Employees who receive less benefit may not be motivated (1) resulting in lower productivity. (1)
- It can create conflict/lead to corruption (1) if allocated unfairly. (1)
- Fringe benefits are additional costs (1) that may result in cash flow problems. (1)
- Decreases business profits, (1) as incentive/package/remuneration costs are higher. (1)
- Administrative costs increase, (1) as benefits need to be correctly recorded for tax purposes. (1)
- Workers only stay with the business for fringe benefits, (1) and may not be committed/loyal to the tasks/business. (1)
- Businesses have to pay advisors/attorneys (1) to help them create benefit plans that comply with legislation. (1)
- Errors in benefit plans (1) may lead to costly lawsuits/regulatory fines. (1)
- Any other relevant answer related to negative impact/disadvantages of fringe benefits on businesses.
Max (6)

subQuestions.questionText:
Read the scenario below and answer the questions that follow.

KIMOL MANUFACTURER (KM)
Kimol Manufacturer implements total quality management (TQM) to reduce the cost of quality. The production manager works closely with suppliers to improve the standards of raw materials. KM monitors their maintenance programmes on a regular basis to prevent the breakdown of equipment. They also provide annual bonuses to employees who meet their sales targets.

Quote TWO ways in which total quality management (TQM) reduces the cost of quality at KM from the scenario above.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 1 mark per correct quote from scenario (mark first 2 only). Max 2 marks.
- The production manager works closely with suppliers to improve the standards of raw materials. (1)
- KM monitors their maintenance programmes on a regular basis to prevent the breakdown of equipment. (1)

NOTE:
1. Mark the first TWO (2) only.
2. Only award marks for responses that are quoted from the scenario.
(2 x 1 = 2)
(NB: Annual bonuses for sales targets relate to motivation, not TQM cost-of-quality reduction.)

subQuestions.questionText: Discuss other ways in which total quality management (TQM) can reduce the cost of quality.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 1 mark for fact + 1 mark for explanation (2 marks per complete way). Max 4 marks.

Other ways TQM can reduce the cost of quality:
- Introduce quality circles (1) to discuss ways of improving the quality of work/workmanship. (1)
- Schedule activities (1) to eliminate duplication of tasks. (1)
- Share responsibility for quality output (1) amongst management and workers. (1)
- Train employees at all levels, (1) so that everyone understands their roles in quality management. (1)
- Develop work systems (1) that empower employees to find new ways of improving quality. (1)
- Improve communication about quality challenges/deviations, (1) so that everyone can learn from experience. (1)
- Reduce investment on expensive, (1) but ineffective inspection procedures in the production process. (1)
- Any other relevant answer related to other ways in which TQM can reduce the cost of quality.

NOTE: Do not award marks for responses that are quoted from the scenario in QUESTION 4.7.1.
Max (4)

subQuestions.questionText: Advise businesses on how the quality of performance of the administration function can contribute to the success of the business.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks per complete way (1 mark for phrase). Max 4 marks.

Quality of performance of administration function:
- Fast and reliable data capturing and processing systems. (2)
- Make reliable information available to management on time. (2)
- Make relevant information available for quick decision-making. (2)
- Handle complaints quickly and effectively. (2)
- Use modern technology efficiently. (2)
- Implement effective risk management policies to minimise business losses. (2)
- Quality assurance/Control/Evaluation is recorded accurately. (2)
- All documentation is kept neatly and orderly in a safe place. (2)
- Easy to recall and find information/documentation. (2)
- Financial documents are kept up to date and recorded accurately. (2)
- All systems and processes are documented. (2)
- Any other relevant answer related to how the quality of performance of the administration function can contribute to the success of the business.
Max (4)

questions.title: SECTION C - BUSINESS ENVIRONMENTS (LEGISLATION) - Consumer Protection Act Essay

subQuestions.questionText:
Businesses are required to have a sound knowledge of the Consumer Protection Act (CPA), 2008 (Act 68 of 2008). The implementation of this Act directly impacts on business operations. Businesses must observe the consumer rights as outlined in the CPA and also comply with this Act.

Write an essay on the Consumer Protection Act in which you include the following aspects:
• Outline the purpose of the Consumer Protection Act.
• Discuss the impact of the Consumer Protection Act on businesses.
• Explain any THREE consumer rights in terms of the CPA.
• Suggest ways in which businesses can comply with the CPA.
subQuestions.memoText:
ESSAY MARK BREAKDOWN: Content (32) + Insight (8) = 40

INTRODUCTION (Max 2 marks; any 2 x 1)
- The Consumer Protection Act aims to protect consumers from exploitation and unfair business practices. (1)
- The CPA was introduced to promote equality in the consumer market for all consumers of goods and services. (1)
- Businesses have a legal responsibility to protect/promote the rights of consumers, as they are held accountable for their actions. (1)
- Businesses that comply with the CPA are able to reduce heavy penalties which may prevent a financial loss in the long term. (1)
- Any other relevant introduction.

5.2 PURPOSE OF THE CPA (Max 10)
2 marks per complete sentence:
- Promotes fair/accessible and sustainable places for people to sell their products. (2)
- Establishes national standards to protect consumers regardless of their economic status. (2)
- Provides guidelines for better consumer information and to prohibit unfair business practices. (2)
- Promotes responsible consumer behaviour amongst consumers. (2)
- Promotes consistent laws relating to consumer transactions and agreements. (2)
- Establishes a National Consumer Commission (NCC). (2)
- Ensures that consumers have access to information they need to make informed choices. (2)
- Promotes the rights and full participation of historically disadvantaged individuals as consumers. (2)
- Ensures that consumers are not misled/deceived by suppliers of goods/services. (2)
- Promotes consumer safety by protecting them from hazardous products/services. (2)
- Strengthens a culture of consumer rights and responsibilities. (2)
- Empowers consumers to take legal action if their rights are not upheld. (2)
- Protects consumers against contracts that include unfair terms, which limit the liability of suppliers. (2)
- Protects consumers against unscrupulous businesses such as fly-by-night franchisors. (2)
- Allows for consumers and businesses to resolve disputes fairly/effectively. (2)
Max (10)

5.3 IMPACT OF THE CPA ON BUSINESSES (Max 14)
1 mark fact + 1 mark explanation per impact:
Positives/Advantages
- Businesses may be safeguarded (1) from dishonest competitors. (1)
- Businesses may be protected (1) if they are regarded as consumers. (1)
- Prevents larger businesses (1) from undermining smaller ones. (1)
- May gain consumer loyalty, (1) if they comply with CPA. (1)
- Enables businesses to resolve disputes fairly (1) through the National Consumer Commission/Consumer Court/Industrial ombudsmen. (1)
- Businesses may build a good image (1) if they ensure that they do not violate consumer rights. (1)
AND/OR
Negatives/Disadvantages
- Confidential business information (1) may become available to competitors. (1)
- Penalties for non-compliance (1) may be very high. (1)
- Businesses may feel unnecessarily burdened (1) by legal processes. (1)
- They have to disclose more information (1) about their products and processes/services. (1)
- Processes and procedures required by CPA (1) can be expensive/time consuming. (1)
- Consumers can take advantage of the business (1) and return goods when it is not necessary to do so. (1)
- Staff need to be trained/Legal experts need to be consulted, (1) which can lead to an increase in operational costs. (1)
- Many business documents need to be simplified/revamped at extra cost (1) as consumers have a right to receive contracts in a simple/understandable language. (1)
- Administration costs increase (1) as legal contracts need to be worded in plain language/pitched at the level of the consumer. (1)
- Businesses may need insurance (1) against claims from consumers (1)/Provisions in the Act increase risks (1) for unforeseen claims and lawsuits. (1)
- Businesses have to replace/repair faulty items/refund money (1) if the fault occurs within six months after purchase. (1)
- Supply chain management in stock levels will have to change, (1) as defective goods have to be replaced within six months at the request of the consumer. (1)
- Information technology systems need to be improved (1) as the retailer must keep more detailed records of interactions with consumers/be able to report to NCC. (1)
Max (14)

5.4 CONSUMER RIGHTS - any THREE (Max 12; 4 marks per right: 2 for right + 2 for explanation; Submax 4 each)

5.4.1 Right to choose (2): choose suppliers/goods (1)+(1); shop around for prices (1)+(1); return unsafe/defective goods for refund (1)+(1); reject goods not same as sample (1)+(1); cancel/renew fixed term agreements (1)+(1); request written quotations and cost estimates (1)+(1). Submax (4)

5.4.2 Right to privacy (2): stop/restrict unwanted direct marketing (1)+(1); object to unwanted promotional emails/telesales (1)+(1); stop/lodge complaints about sharing personal details (1)+(1). Submax (4)

5.4.3 Right to fair and honest dealings (2): suppliers may not use force/harass (1)+(1); not give misleading info (1)+(1); not promote pyramid/chain-letter schemes (1)+(1); not overbook/oversell (1)+(1). Submax (4)

5.4.4 Right to disclosure and information (2): plain language contracts (1)+(1); display fully inclusive prices (1)+(1); correct labelling (1)+(1); request unit/bulk price (1)+(1); pay lower price if two displayed (1)+(1); disclose country of origin/expiry/ingredients (1)+(1). Submax (4)

5.4.5 Right to fair and responsible marketing (2): not mislead on pricing/benefits/uses (1)+(1); cancel direct marketing purchases within 5-day cooling-off period (1)+(1). Submax (4)

5.4.6 Right to fair value/good quality and safety (2): demand quality (1)+(1); receive implied/written warranty (1)+(1); informed about hazardous products (1)+(1); reject goods not same quality as sample (1)+(1); return faulty items within 6 months (1)+(1). Submax (4)

5.4.7 Right to accountability by suppliers (2): protected in lay-bye agreements (1)+(1); honour credit vouchers and prepaid services (1)+(1). Submax (4)

5.4.8 Right to fair/just and reasonable terms and conditions (2): written notices of clauses limiting rights (1)+(1); not market/sell at unfair prices (1)+(1). Submax (4)

5.4.9 Right to equality in the consumer market (2): not limit access (1)+(1); not vary quality between consumers (1)+(1); not discriminate when marketing in different areas (1)+(1); not charge different prices (1)+(1); quality may not vary between consumers (1)+(1). Submax (4)

NOTE: Mark the first THREE (3) only. Max (12)

5.5 WAYS BUSINESSES CAN COMPLY WITH CPA (Max 10)
2 marks per complete way:
- Disclose prices of all products on sale. (2)
- Provide adequate training to staff on the CPA. (2)
- All agreements must provide for a five-day cooling-off period. (2)
- Ensure that goods/services offered are standardised/of the same quality. (2)
- Comply with the requirements regarding promotional competitions. (2)
- Comply with requirements regarding the display of information on labels/packaging. (2)
- Display the name of the business on all business documents, such as invoices/contracts. (2)
- Bundling of goods/services should benefit consumers, such as offering a cell phone and a tablet at a special price. (2)
- Implement measures that will facilitate complaints, such as suggestion boxes. (2)
Max (10)

CONCLUSION (Max 2; any 1 x 2)
- The Consumer Protection Act requires both businesses and consumers to act responsibly when conducting business activities in the consumer market. (2)
- Businesses that correctly implement the CPA are able to gain the positive impact and reduce the negative impact on their business operations. (2)
- Businesses that apply the consumer rights are able to increase market share, gain more loyal customers and improve their customer base. (2)
- Compliance with CPA not only benefits consumers but also strengthens the overall integrity of the market by ensuring a balanced relationship between consumers and businesses. (2)
- Any other relevant conclusion.

ESSAY BREAKDOWN OF MARKS:
- Introduction: 2
- Purpose of CPA: 10
- Impact on businesses: 14
- Consumer rights (any 3): 12
- Ways to comply: 10
- Conclusion: 2
- Content max: 32

INSIGHT (8 marks):
- Layout (L): 2 (intro, paragraphs, conclusion present)
- Analysis/Interpretation (A): 2 (1 mark all headings addressed; 1 mark interpretation 16-32 marks)
- Synthesis (S): 2 (relevant facts/decisions based on question)
- Originality (O): 2 (recent examples not older than 2 years in any 2 of 4 sub-questions)

LASO: Allocate 2 if all met, 1 if some met, 0 if none met.

TOTAL: 32 (Content) + 8 (Insight) = 40

questions.title: SECTION C - BUSINESS OPERATIONS (HUMAN RESOURCES FUNCTION) Essay

subQuestions.questionText:
Businesses apply the recruitment procedure when advertising vacant positions and they are required to understand the impact of external recruitment. Interviewers need to be aware of their role while conducting interviews. Businesses and employees must familiarise themselves with the reasons for the termination of employment contracts.

Write an essay on the human resources function in which you include the following aspects:
• Outline the recruitment procedure as a human resources activity.
• Explain the impact of external recruitment on businesses.
• Discuss the role of the interviewer during the interview.
• Advise businesses on reasons for the termination of an employment contract.
subQuestions.memoText:
ESSAY MARK BREAKDOWN: Content (32) + Insight (8) = 40

INTRODUCTION (Max 2 marks; any 2 x 1)
- Recruitment procedure is a systematic process on identifying and filling vacant positions within the business. (1)
- External recruitment enables businesses to employ qualified people from outside the business. (1)
- The interviewer is responsible for administration and logistical arrangements of the interview process. (1)
- The reasons for the termination of employment contracts should be clearly explained to all employees. (1)
- Any other relevant introduction.

6.2 RECRUITMENT PROCEDURE (Max 12)
2 marks per complete step:
- The HR manager should evaluate the job/prepare a job analysis, that includes the job specification/job description, in order to identify recruitment needs. (2)
- The HR manager should prepare the job description in order to determine the responsibility/key performance areas related to the nature of the job. (2)
- The HR manager should indicate the job specification/description/key performance areas to attract suitable candidates. (2)
- Choose the method of recruitment, such as internal/external, to reach/target the suitable applicants/candidates. (2)
- Vacancies can be internally advertised via internal email/word of mouth/posters/staff notices. (2)
- If internal recruitment is unsuccessful, external recruitment should be considered. (2)
- If the external recruitment is chosen, the relevant recruitment sources should be selected, such as recruitment agencies/tertiary institutions/newspapers. (2)
- The advertisement should be prepared with the relevant information, such as the name of the company/contact details/contact person. (2)
- Place the advertisement in the appropriate media that will ensure that the best candidates apply. (2)
- Any other relevant answer.
NOTE: The procedure can be in any order. Max (12)

6.3 IMPACT OF EXTERNAL RECRUITMENT (Max 12)
1 mark fact + 1 mark explanation per impact:
Positives/Advantages
- New candidates bring new talents/ideas/experiences/skills (1) into the business. (1)/Overall efficiency/Increase in productivity may occur (1) as new workers add value to the business. (1)
- There is a larger pool of candidates (1) from which to choose. (1)
- It may help the business to meet affirmative action (1) and BBBEE targets. (1)
- Minimises unhappiness/conflict amongst current employees (1) who may have applied for the post. (1)
- There is a better chance of getting a suitable candidate with the required skills/qualifications/competencies (1) who do not need much training/development which reduces costs. (1)
AND/OR
Negatives/Disadvantages
- Information on CVs/from referees (1) may not be reliable. (1)
- Many unsuitable applications (1) can slow down the selection process. (1)
- New candidates generally take longer to adjust (1) to a new work environment. (1)
- External sources can be expensive, (1) such as recruitment agencies' fees/advertisements in newspapers/magazines. (1)
- The selection process may not be effective (1) as an incompetent candidate may be chosen. (1)
- Recruitment process takes longer (1) as background checks must be conducted (1)/is time-consuming (1) due to the lengthy process of finding suitable candidates. (1)
- In-service training may be needed (1) which decreases productivity during the time of training. (1)
- External recruitment may limit promotion/growth opportunities for existing employees (1) that could lead to resentment. (1)
Max (12)

6.4 ROLE OF THE INTERVIEWER (Max 12)
1 mark fact + 1 mark explanation per role:
- Allocate the same amount of time (1) to each candidate. (1)
- Introduce members of the interviewing panel (1) to each candidate/interviewee. (1)
- Make the interviewee feel at ease (1) to acquire good responses. (1)
- Explain the purpose of the interview (1) to the panel and the interviewee. (1)
- Record interviewees' responses (1) for future reference. (1)
- Do not misinform/mislead the interviewee (1) by asking unrelated questions to the position. (1)
- Avoid discriminatory/controversial (1) types of questions. (1)
- Provide an opportunity for the interviewee to ask questions (1) about the position/job. (1)
- Close the interview by thanking the interviewee (1) for attending the interview. (1)
- Any other relevant answer.
Max (12)

6.5 REASONS FOR TERMINATION OF EMPLOYMENT CONTRACT (Max 10)
2 marks per complete reason:
- The employer may dismiss an employee for a valid reason(s), such as unsatisfactory job performance/misconduct. (2)
- Employer may no longer have work for redundant employees/cannot fulfil the contract/is restructuring. (2)
- The employer may retrench some employees due to insolvency/may not be able to pay the employees. (2)
- Employees decided to leave/resign voluntarily for better job opportunities. (2)
- An employee may have reached the pre-determined age for retirement. (2)
- Incapacity to work due to illness/injuries. (2)
- By a mutual agreement between the employer and employee. (2)
- The duration of the employment contract expires/comes to an end. (2)
- Any other relevant answer.
Max (10)

CONCLUSION (Max 2; any 1 x 2)
- Businesses that implement effective recruitment procedures are able to achieve their recruitment goals. (2)
- A business that uses external recruitment methods is able to ensure a diversified workforce. (2)
- The interviewer who understands their role during the interview will be able to successfully conduct effective interviews. (2)
- The HR manager should be knowledgeable on the reasons for terminating an employment contract to avoid unnecessary lawsuits/civil proceedings. (2)
- Any other relevant conclusion.

ESSAY BREAKDOWN OF MARKS:
- Introduction: 2
- Recruitment procedure: 12
- Impact of external recruitment: 12
- Role of interviewer: 12
- Reasons for termination: 10
- Conclusion: 2
- Content max: 32

INSIGHT (8 marks):
- Layout (L): 2 (intro, paragraphs, conclusion present)
- Analysis/Interpretation (A): 2 (1 mark all headings addressed; 1 mark interpretation 16-32 marks)
- Synthesis (S): 2 (relevant facts/decisions based on question)
- Originality (O): 2 (recent examples not older than 2 years in any 2 of 4 sub-questions)

LASO: Allocate 2 if all met, 1 if some met, 0 if none met.

TOTAL: 32 (Content) + 8 (Insight) = 40
